Not all this material is suitable for PV glass, because less than 0.1% iron oxide content is required, either from naturally low impurities or use of cleaning processes (Thomsen et al. 2009; Heidari and Anctil 2022). The geographic distribution of high-purity SiO deposits has resulted in illegal mining, 2 mostly in Asia, but the U.S. resource of high-quality sands is advantageous (Heidari and Anctil 2022; United Nations Environment Programme 2019). Carefully separated cullet, both pre- and post-consumer, can help offset demands on this natural resource. • Soda ash and lime: The United States produces approximately 12 million t of soda ash, nearly half of which goes toward glass manufacturing, and imports very little (Bolen 2022). The United States produces approximately 16 million t of lime, with minimal imports (U.S. Geological Survey 2025b). • Antimony: Antimony (Sb) is used as an additive—at a concentration of less than 0.01% (Thomsen et al. 2009)—in rolled glass production to control the oxidation state of iron for improved transmission and reduce bubbles (Hubert 2015; Chen et al. 2020; Blieske and Stollwerck 2013). Antimony oxide must only be used in rolled glass production and cannot be added to float production, because it would react with the tin bath to create tin oxide particles (Blieske and Stollwerck 2013; Thomsen et al. 2009). Cerium oxide34 or arsenic oxide can substitute for antimony (Hubert 2015; Thomsen et al. 2009). • Equipment: Industry interviews indicated that turnkey rolled glass manufacturing lines are available for purchase in the United States. 34 Cerium also absorbs hard ultraviolet light that would otherwise degrade PV cells and/or encapsulation. 50 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 3 Cadmium Telluride Modules 3.1 Overview Globally, CdTe modules represented approximately 2% of all PV modules produced in 2024 (PV Tech Research 2025) and approximately 18% of U.S. PV installations (21% of U.S. utility-scale PV installations) (U.S. Energy Information Administration 2025a). As of 2024, one company (First Solar) was the only large-scale producer of CdTe modules. In 2024, there was approximately 22.0 GW of CdTe PV manufacturing capacity globally (8.9 dc GW in the United States) and about 15.5 GW of production (6.3 GW in the United States) dc dc dc (PV Tech Research 2025). The primary source of unutilized capacity was approximately 5 GW dc of new capacity ramping in the United States and India. First Solar plans to expand U.S. and global manufacturing capacity to 14 GW (all Series 7) and 25 GW , respectively, by 2026, and dc dc sales to between 15.5 GW and 19.3 GW by 2025 (First Solar 2025a). First Solar indicates that dc dc Series 7 modules produced in the United States have 100% domestic sources for components listed in the U.S. Treasury domestic content guidance. While First Solar’s Vietnamese and Malaysian CdTe module manufacturing facilities remain active, U.S. CdTe module imports from those countries fell in 2024 by 15%.
